meta.purpose: locate delta_sig with a directional criterion, and score two interval procedures against one target
meta.criterion_for_delta_sig: P(CI upper limit < 1) on the benefit side, i.e. the probability of successfully declaring the benefit
meta.criterion_rejected: the plain two-sided Wald rejection rate, which is not monotone in delta: it dips at delta_tip and rises again past it, so a bisection on it returns the search boundary rather than a crossing
meta.search_domain: [0, delta_tip] per cell, with the cap recorded as a first-class field
meta.coverage_target: the between-group true log odds ratio, identical for both layers
meta.coverage_delta_rationale: coverage answers whether the interval recovers the effect the study targets, which is a property of the measurement model rather than of the asymmetry; the effect of delta on the interval is characterised in block 1
meta.seed_note: each bisection evaluation gets its own stream so the two bracket endpoints are not correlated

checks.question: is P(CI upper < 1) monotone decreasing on [0, delta_tip], and does the two-sided rate really rise past delta_tip?
checks.why_both_parts_must_hold: the first part says the bisection is valid. The second says the alternative really is invalid, so the docstring claim is evidence rather than assertion. A check that passed merely because the criterion is monotone would leave the reason unverified

checks.question: is every reported delta_sig a located crossing rather than an edge of the search domain?
checks.rule: a cell is either bracketed -- criterion at delta = 0 at or above alpha and criterion at delta_tip below alpha -- or explicitly capped. Returning delta_tip as a located value is forbidden

checks.question: is delta_sig at or below delta_tip in every cell?
checks.note: this is a property of the decreasing criterion on a closed domain, not an empirical finding; the check exists so that a future change to the criterion cannot quietly break it

checks.question: at delta_tip, is P(CI upper < 1) close to alpha/2 rather than to alpha?
checks.derivation: at delta_tip the population observed OR is exactly 1, so the two-sided test rejects with probability alpha split evenly between the two directions; the directional criterion counts only the benefit direction, hence alpha/2

checks.question: is every cell searched on [0, its own delta_tip], with no bisection step falling outside?
checks.rule: the upper limit of the search is delta_tip of the same cell, and every evaluated delta lies in [0, delta_tip]. Past delta_tip the observed odds ratio is on the harm side and the criterion no longer measures whether a benefit can be declared

checks.question: can the cap branch fire on this grid, and is its decision predicate correct?

predicate_unit_test.none_case: handled upstream by an early return, so the predicate is never applied to None

checks.honesty_note: the cap branch is NOT exercised end to end by this grid and is not claimed to be. The criterion at delta_tip is structurally about alpha/2, so the branch is dead code here. What is verified is the decision predicate, by unit test. The branch is retained because a grid with a wider interval relative to delta_tip, or a criterion that failed to fall, would reach it, and in that case a silent boundary return is the specific failure this project has already produced once
checks.why_this_check_exists: an earlier version of the probe recomputed the cap decision inside the check, so it kept passing with the branch disabled -- verifying the arithmetic rather than the branch. This version reports unreachability as a finding and tests the predicate separately
